entries.title: NTDS.dit
entries.summary: NTDS.dit is the Active Directory database on a domain controller and contains credential-derived material for domain accounts.
entries.significance: Direct access usually requires high privilege on a domain controller. That makes attempted access, snapshot creation, unusual backup activity and staging on a domain controller high-value signals. See the [defensive reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/vss/in-box-vss-writers) for the authoritative model. Copies outside the live directory can be easier to reach. Protect system-state backups, hypervisor snapshots and recovery media with the same seriousness as the domain controllers themselves. Defender view: Record the owning system, approved readers, protection method, backup locations and the telemetry that proves access.
triage: Volume Shadow Copy or system-state backup activity outside the expected schedule.
Unusual processes, remote sessions or administrative shares on a domain controller.
Access to the NTDS directory or registry hive backups by an unapproved account or process.
Large archive or database files staged in temporary, public or administrative-share locations.
Follow-on authentication from new systems using privileged or service accounts from the affected domain.
entries.caveats: Do not assume that the filename alone proves theft. Confirm the source, access method, destination and whether the action matches an approved backup or recovery task. Do not focus only on the live path. A copied virtual disk, system-state backup or domain controller snapshot can contain the same sensitive material.

Monitoring should cover the live store and the less protected copies created by backup, deployment and troubleshooting workflows. See the [defensive reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/get-started/virtual-dc/active-directory-domain-services-overview) for the authoritative model. Defender view: Record the owning system, approved readers, protection method, backup locations and the telemetry that proves access.
triage: Access by an unusual process, account, host or workload.
Copy, export, snapshot or backup activity outside an approved workflow.
Privilege changes or security-control changes shortly before access.
Follow-on authentication or data access using material linked to the artefact.
New copies in temporary, staging, archive or cloud-storage locations.
entries.caveats: Do not assume that finding SSH private keys proves theft. Confirm the reader, access type, destination, subsequent use and whether the operation matches a documented administrative task.

entries.summary: Terraform state files can expose deployed infrastructure values, resource identifiers and sometimes provider or application secrets.
entries.significance: Access often marks a transition from initial compromise to durable reach or collection. Combine the [defensive guidance](https://www.cisa.gov/topics/cyber-threats-and-advisories) with local ownership, backup and rotation records. Defender view: Record the owning system, approved readers, storage and backup locations, rotation method and telemetry proving access.
triage: Access by an unusual process, identity, workload or administrative path.
Copy, export, snapshot, archive or backup activity outside an approved workflow.
Permission, policy or security-control changes shortly before access.
New copies in temporary, shared, removable or cloud-storage locations.
Follow-on authentication or resource access using linked material.
entries.caveats: Do not assume that discovering Terraform state files proves theft. Confirm the reader, access type, destination, subsequent use and whether the complete operation matches a documented task.
